title: C. Grouping and hierarchy
definition: Frames group ideas by meaning, are titled accurately, keep unrelated concepts apart, and make the main idea vs supporting detail visible. Frames are not word-count buckets.
questions: Are important relationships between frames visible?
Is the hierarchy (main idea → supporting detail) useful for understanding?

severity.critical: An expected frame is missing, or two concepts the case requires apart share a frame; a limit sits in a different frame from its claim.
severity.major: A card in the wrong frame; over-fragmentation (frame_count above the case's bound); an example weighted above its main idea.
severity.minor: A frame title that is vague but not wrong.

model_judge: Rubric score 1–5: 'Does each frame hold one coherent subject, titled by what it is about?'
human: Reviewer confirms frame boundaries in the canvas spec make sense for the audience

requiredAssertions: together/apart for each pair in canvas.together / keepSeparate
passCriteria: All critical grouping assertions pass and the judged score is ≥ 4.
failCriteria: A critical grouping assertion fails, or the judged score is ≤ 2.
passExample: RAG source: frames 'Retrieval signals', 'Fusion and candidates', 'Reranking', 'Generation', 'Trade-offs'; the RRF formula sits in Fusion; the trade-off table stands alone.
failExample: Frames 'Part 1', 'Part 2', 'Part 3' cut every 300 words; reranking and BM25 share a frame; the example is the biggest card.

judgeScale.meaning: Mostly coherent; one misplaced idea or one vague title.
Every frame is one coherent subject with an accurate title; the main idea of each is obvious.
